messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty INF-4621 — Multiple nodes in `infer-pool-usw` reported NotReady and kubelet restarts within the last 2m. Affected pods show container exits with `CUDA_ERROR_DEVICE_RESET` and occasional OOMs. Alerts: node_heartbeat_loss x5, node_kubelet_restart x5. Dash: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/infra/inferpool-usw
ben (oncall): on it. I'm pulling logs now. pinging infra and runtime.
carla: ack. grabbing kubelet logs from one of the NotReady nodes (10.12.34.56)
ben (oncall): `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep infer-pool-usw`

```
ip-10-12-34-56   NotReady   <none>   48m   v1.28.1   gpu:2   us-west1
ip-10-12-34-57   NotReady   <none>   47m   v1.28.1   gpu:2   us-west1
ip-10-12-34-58   Ready      <none>   4h    v1.28.1   gpu:2   us-west1
...
```
carla: from journalctl on ip-10-12-34-56:
```
Mar 15 03:12:02 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 31415 (redwood-runtime) total-vm: 1023456kB, anon-rss: 850000kB
Mar 15 03:12:03 kubelet[1234]: kubelet: runtime service crashed, restarting
Mar 15 03:12:05 nvidia: GPU 0: GPU reset detected
```
ml-runtime: seeing repeated `CUDA_ERROR_DEVICE_RESET` across pods on the node; containers crash loop with exit code 137 and GPU resets around same timestamp.
alice-cust-ops: customers: partial 95th latency spikes (approx +400ms) and increased 5xx rate on hosted endpoints backed by infer-pool-usw. CS already getting first reports.
ben (oncall): mitigation plan — short term:
- cordon & drain the 2 NotReady nodes (if they become Ready briefly, drain pods)
- scale up warm replacement nodes in us-west (request to infra)
- route new requests away from infer-pool-usw to eu-west fallback for critical customers
- pin recent kubelet config change in rollback if we find correlation
carla: trying `kubectl drain ip-10-12-34-56 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force` but drain failing: pod `redwood-runtime` stuck Terminating with `preStop` timeout. logs attached.
ben (oncall): ok force-evict via `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0 --force` for stuck runtime pods, we prefer to avoid data loss but need availability.
infra-bot: new node provisioning requested: pool=infer-usw, count=3, request_id=infra-req-8732. ETA ~120s.
sre-lead: checking recent infra changes — there was an automated kernel update pushed to infer nodes last night (k8s node image v2026.03.14-kernel-5.19). Could be related.
ml-runtime: also seeing increase in GPU ECC errors prior to reset. Pulling `nvidia-smi` history.
carla: grabbing `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200` and `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` from node.
```
Mar 15 03:11:58 kubelet[1234]: E03015 03:11:58 kubelet.go:2565] SyncLoop (PLEG): "redwood-runtime_default/abc-123", event: &pleg.ContainerRestart
Mar 15 03:12:02 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 31415 (redwood-runtime)
Mar 15 03:12:03 kubelet[1234]: NodeLease: lost heartbeat to control plane
```
ben (oncall): routing update: applying temporary routing policy to move non-dedicated traffic away from infer-pool-usw. `routingctl set-priority infer-usw --drain --exclude-critical=false`
alice-cust-ops: notified top 10 affected accounts via status page draft. CS on standby.
infra-bot: 3 new nodes launched and joined cluster: ip-10-12-34-80..82. Autoscaler adjusted replica set.
ben (oncall): once new nodes are Ready, we'll scale up `infer-runtime` deployment to spread load. Also adding `podAntiAffinity` for heavy pods to avoid co-locating GPU drivers.
carla: note — kernel OOM + GPU reset pattern looks like memory leak in runtime + driver instability. collecting heap profiles from failing pods where possible.
ml-runtime: quick check: the container images were rolled 6h ago (runtime v2.4.1). Not seeing obvious mem leak in last release notes but will run local stress test.
next-oncall: I'm next oncall in 45m, happy to take handoff. planning to stay for 1h after handoff.
ben (oncall): handoff: I'm handing to @next-oncall. Current state: 2 nodes NotReady (evicted), 3 replacement nodes joined, routing in fallback for non-critical. Customer impact reduced but residual 95th latency still +80ms. Action items: monitor for new kubelet restarts, confirm rollback of kernel package if correlation confirmed, own postmortem. Logs and artifacts stored in incident doc INF-4621 (link).
next-oncall: taking it. I'll keep shift. please add me to zoom with infra if we need direct node access.
alice-cust-ops: status page updated: "Degraded performance for inference in us-west. Failover in progress."
ben (oncall): closing loop — filing follow-up ticket to investigate kernel update + nvidia driver compatibility; owner: @ml-runtime; postmortem owner: @ben. Will keep this thread for notes. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INF-4621 acknowledged by next-oncall. Postmortem template created: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/INF-4621
carla: quick note — saved `dmesg` and `kubelet` logs to /var/lib/incident/INF-4621-logs.tar.gz, uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/INF-4621/ (restricted access)
next-oncall: monitoring: all new nodes stable for 10m, no additional GPU resets. I'll schedule a deeper memory-debug run overnight and update postmortem draft tomorrow."
